words.enDefinition: A website showing prices for the same or similar products from several sellers.

examples.en: I used a price comparison site to see which store had the cheapest desk lamp.
examples.zh: 我用「比价网站」查看哪家店的台灯最便宜。

examples.en: The price comparison site showed three offers for the exact calculator model listed on my syllabus.
examples.zh: 「比价网站」显示了课程大纲上那款计算器的三家报价。

collocations: list a product on a price comparison site

words.enDefinition: A tool that monitors how the price of an item changes over time.

examples.en: I put the headphones into a price tracker while I waited for my next paycheck.
examples.zh: 发下一次工资前，我把那副耳机加进了「价格追踪工具」。

examples.en: The price tracker picked up a change in the cost of the lamp late last night.
examples.zh: 「价格追踪工具」昨晚很晚才检测到台灯价格变化。

collocations: add an item to a price tracker

words.enDefinition: A record of the prices charged for an item at different times.

examples.en: The price history showed that the speaker had cost less earlier in the semester.
examples.zh: 「历史价格记录」显示，这款音箱在本学期早些时候更便宜。

examples.en: I checked the price history to see whether the advertised discount looked unusual for that backpack.
examples.zh: 我查看了「历史价格记录」，想知道这款背包标出的折扣力度是否少见。

collocations: a chart of the price history

words.enDefinition: A message sent when a watched item changes price or reaches a chosen price.

examples.en: I set a price alert for the calculator before I left the library that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午离开图书馆前，我设置了计算器的「价格变动提醒」。

examples.en: The price alert arrived during class, so I waited until the break to check it.
examples.zh: 「价格变动提醒」是在上课时收到的，所以我等到课间才查看。

collocations: a price alert for a laptop

words.enDefinition: A noticeable increase in the price of something.

examples.en: The price hike meant the refill cartridges cost more than the whole printer during last year's sale.
examples.zh: 「价格大幅上涨」后，替换墨盒比去年促销时的整台打印机还贵。

examples.en: There was a price hike on poster paper just before our final exhibition.
examples.zh: 期末展览前，海报纸的「价格大幅上涨」。

collocations: a price hike on basic supplies

words.enDefinition: The cheapest price in the available record for an item.

examples.en: The tracking chart showed that the lamp had hit an all-time low that morning.
examples.zh: 追踪图表显示，这款台灯当天上午达到了「历史最低价」。

examples.en: I bought the speaker after the site flagged its price as an all-time low.
examples.zh: 网站提示音箱达到了「历史最低价」后，我买了它。

collocations: an all-time low for this model

words.enDefinition: The minimum price shown in the previous thirty days for an item.
acceptedEnVariants: lowest price in the last 30 days

examples.en: The product page showed the lowest price in 30 days beneath the current selling price.
examples.zh: 商品页在当前售价下方显示了「近30天最低价」。

examples.en: I compared the sale price with the lowest price in 30 days on the chart.
examples.zh: 我把促销价跟图表上的「近30天最低价」作了比较。

collocations: show the lowest price in 30 days
a label stating lowest price in 30 days
compare with the lowest price in 30 days

words.enDefinition: The price set when a product first becomes available to buy.

examples.en: The launch price was higher than the amount now shown for the same keyboard online.
examples.zh: 这款键盘「上市时的价格」比目前网上显示的同款价格高。

examples.en: A review from last year mentioned the launch price of the lamp I wanted.
examples.zh: 去年一条评价提到我想买的台灯「上市时的价格」。

words.enDefinition: The span between the lowest and highest prices being considered.

examples.en: I set a price range before browsing lamps because my dorm desk only needed something simple.
examples.zh: 我在浏览台灯之前设好了「价格区间」，因为宿舍书桌有盏简单的台灯就够了。

examples.en: Most of the scientific calculators in my price range were suitable for the course.
examples.zh: 在我能接受的「价格区间」内，大部分科学计算器都适合这门课。

collocations: a price range for student laptops

words.enDefinition: Indicates that a seller gives the price only when someone asks.

examples.en: The custom poster frame was marked “Price on request” on the art shop's website.
examples.zh: 美术用品店网站上，定制海报框标着「价格请询问」。

examples.en: I saw “Price on request” next to the larger display boards in the seller's catalogue.
examples.zh: 我在卖家目录的大号展示板旁看到了「价格请询问」。

collocations: a listing saying price on request
a label reading price on request

words.enDefinition: To arrange a list of products according to how much they cost.

examples.en: I chose to sort by price after limiting the results to the correct calculator model.
examples.zh: 我把结果筛到只剩正确的计算器型号后，选择了「按价格排序」。

examples.en: The site lets me sort by price even when I have several brands selected.
examples.zh: 即使已经选了多个品牌，我仍能在这个网站「按价格排序」。

collocations: a menu to sort by price
sort by price before comparing models

words.enDefinition: A sorting option that lists the least expensive items first.

examples.en: I selected “Price low to high” and found several cheaper cases for my laptop.
examples.zh: 我选了「价格从低到高」，找到了几款更便宜的电脑保护套。

examples.en: The page stayed on “Price low to high” after I removed the filter for color.
examples.zh: 取消颜色筛选后，页面仍然用「价格从低到高」来排序。

collocations: a menu option marked price low to high
sort using price low to high

words.enDefinition: The available choice that costs the least.

examples.en: The cheapest option was a smaller pack, so I checked how many pages it contained.
examples.zh: 「最便宜的选项」是小包装，所以我查看了里面有多少页。

examples.en: I picked the cheapest option that included the cable I needed for my class.
examples.zh: 我选了包含上课所需线缆的「最便宜的选项」。

words.enDefinition: The amount by which one price is higher or lower than another.

examples.en: The price difference was small enough that I chose the larger box for our project.
examples.zh: 「价差」很小，所以我选了大号盒子用于小组项目。

examples.en: I noticed the price difference only after checking what came with each lamp.
examples.zh: 我在核对每盏灯随附的东西后，才注意到「价差」。

collocations: explain the price difference between two models

words.enDefinition: A quick lookup to find or confirm the price of an item.

examples.en: I asked for a price check because the notebook did not have a shelf label.
examples.zh: 那本笔记本没有货架标签，所以我请人帮忙「查价」。

examples.en: The cashier did a price check before ringing up the remaining supplies for our workshop.
examples.zh: 收银员先「查价」，再给研讨活动剩下的用品结算。

words.enDefinition: A comparison using items or offers matched for relevant features and conditions.

examples.en: A like-for-like comparison was possible once I found two pens with the same number of refills.
examples.zh: 找到两支附带相同数量替芯的笔后，我才能「按同等条件比较」。

examples.en: We checked the delivery terms before making a like-for-like comparison of the two desk chairs.
examples.zh: 我们先核对配送条件，再对两把书桌椅「按同等条件比较」。

collocations: a like-for-like comparison of two offers

words.enDefinition: A comparison showing that one thing costs double the amount of another.

examples.en: The larger lamp costs twice as much as the one I use at home.
examples.zh: 大款台灯的「价格是我在家用的那款的两倍」。

examples.en: This cover costs twice as much, although both versions fit the same tablet model.
examples.zh: 虽然两个版本都适配同款平板，但这款保护套的「价格是两倍」。

collocations: costs twice as much as the smaller one

words.enDefinition: At a price equal to the one being compared or discussed.

examples.en: Another shop offered a larger pack for the same price, so I checked the sheet count.
examples.zh: 另一家店「以相同价格」出售更大一包，于是我去查看有多少张。

examples.en: I could get the blue case for the same price if I picked it up locally.
examples.zh: 如果在本地自提，我可以「以相同价格」买到蓝色保护套。

collocations: get a bigger pack for the same price
sell two versions for the same price
offer more for the same price

words.enDefinition: The cost of one sheet when a pack price is divided by its sheet count.

examples.en: I calculated the price per sheet because the packs contained different numbers of sheets.
examples.zh: 两包纸张数不同，所以我算了算「每张的价格」。

examples.en: The price per sheet was lower in the larger pack my classmate had found online.
examples.zh: 同学在网上找到的大包装「每张的价格」更低。

words.enDefinition: A label giving a price for a standard volume of one hundred millilitres.

examples.en: The shelf label showed a price per 100 ml below the total for each bottle.
examples.zh: 货架标签在每瓶总价的下方显示了「每100毫升」的价格。

examples.en: I compared the two shampoos per 100 ml because the bottles were different sizes.
examples.zh: 两瓶洗发水大小不同，我按「每100毫升」对比了两种价格。

words.enDefinition: A label giving the amount charged for each pair of items.

examples.en: I checked whether the socks were priced per pair before buying enough for the trip.
examples.zh: 买足旅行要用的袜子前，我核对了是不是「按双计价」。

examples.en: The large text showed the total, and the smaller text showed the cost per pair.
examples.zh: 大字标总价，小字标「每双的价格」。

words.enDefinition: Ends up costing less once the relevant amounts are compared.

examples.en: The refill pack works out cheaper per sheet if I use it for both classes.
examples.zh: 如果两门课都用这个内页补充装，按张「算下来更便宜」。

examples.en: Buying locally works out cheaper once I include the delivery charge from the other shop.
examples.zh: 把另一家店的配送费算进去，在本地买「算下来更便宜」。

words.enDefinition: Describes a price that does not yet include the charge for shipping.

examples.en: The smaller number was the price before shipping, which explained the difference between the two screens.
examples.zh: 小一点的数字是「未计配送费」的价格，这解释了两个页面为什么不同。

examples.en: I noted the cost before shipping, then checked the options for delivery to campus.
examples.zh: 我记下「未计配送费」的价格，然后查看送到校园的配送选项。

words.enDefinition: Describes an amount calculated without any applicable tax added.

examples.en: The smaller figure was the price before tax, according to the breakdown on the screen.
examples.zh: 按页面明细，较小的数字是「税前」价格。

examples.en: I copied the price before tax because our project estimate listed taxes on a separate line.
examples.zh: 我们项目的估算把税单列了一行，所以我抄了「税前」价格。

words.enDefinition: A list showing how the different parts of a price add up.

examples.en: The price breakdown showed separate lines for the notebook, gift wrapping, and the shipping charge.
examples.zh: 「价格组成明细」把笔记本、礼品包装和配送费分别列了三行。

examples.en: I checked the price breakdown before deciding whether to order the supplies with my roommate.
examples.zh: 我先查看「价格组成明细」，再决定要不要跟室友一起订购这些用品。

collocations: check the price breakdown before ordering

words.enDefinition: A price expressed in the currency used in the buyer's current location.

examples.en: I looked for the price in local currency before comparing the two stationery sites.
examples.zh: 比较两个文具网站之前，我先找了「本币标价」。

examples.en: The website displayed the price in local currency beneath the amount in the seller's currency.
examples.zh: 网站在以卖家货币标出的金额下方显示了换算后的「本币标价」。

collocations: display the price in local currency
show the price in local currency
compare the price in local currency

words.enDefinition: The identical product offered at another store or on another website.

examples.en: I checked for the same item elsewhere before buying the cover for my lab notebook.
examples.zh: 在买实验记录本的封套前，我查了查「别处有没有卖同款」。

examples.en: My roommate found the same item elsewhere after searching for the lamp's exact model number.
examples.zh: 室友按准确的台灯型号搜索，「在别处找到了同款」。

collocations: check for the same item elsewhere
see the same item elsewhere for less

words.enDefinition: The extra amount charged for one option compared with a similar alternative.

examples.en: There was a price premium for the padded sleeve, so I checked the difference in materials.
examples.zh: 带加厚夹层的内胆包有「溢价」，所以我查看了两款材料的差别。

examples.en: I did not want to pay a price premium just to get a different color.
examples.zh: 我不想仅为了换个颜色就付「溢价」。

collocations: a price premium for a color

words.enDefinition: An option that serves a similar purpose and costs less.

examples.en: I found a cheaper alternative that fit the same binder and used the same paper size.
examples.zh: 我找到了一个「更便宜的替代品」，适合同一个活页夹，纸张尺寸也一样。

examples.en: My classmate suggested a cheaper alternative when the branded calculator case was outside my budget.
examples.zh: 品牌计算器保护套超出预算时，同学推荐了一个「更便宜的替代品」。

words.enDefinition: Surprise or dismay on discovering that a price is much higher than expected.

examples.en: I felt sticker shock when I saw how much the required calculator cost new.
examples.zh: 看到课上指定计算器的全新售价时，我「被高价吓了一跳」。

examples.en: The cost of the replacement cartridges gave us sticker shock during our project planning.
examples.zh: 规划项目时，替换墨盒的价格让我们「吓了一跳」。

words.enDefinition: Describes an upgrade or alternative whose benefits justify its higher price.

examples.en: We decided the sturdier display board was worth the extra cost for our exhibition.
examples.zh: 我们觉得展览用更牢固的展示板「值得多花这笔钱」。

examples.en: I wasn’t sure the extra dividers were worth the extra cost of the larger binder.
examples.zh: 我不确定大款活页夹多出的这几张隔页「值不值得多花这笔钱」。

collocations: decide whether something is worth the extra cost
consider something worth the extra cost

words.enDefinition: A display comparing a seller’s stated previous price with its current price.

examples.en: The shop used was-now pricing on the sign above the discounted calculators near the entrance.
examples.zh: 店铺在入口旁打折计算器上方的牌子上用了「原价现价对照标示」。

examples.en: The website used was-now pricing, showing the earlier amount above the current price for the lamp.
examples.zh: 网站用了「原价现价对照标示」，在台灯现价上方列出此前的价格。

collocations: show was-now pricing for a sale item

words.enDefinition: An amount shown as a benchmark beside the current selling price.

examples.en: The page showed a compare-at price beside the current amount for the headphones.
examples.zh: 商品页把耳机「标示的参考价」放在当前售价旁边。

examples.en: I checked what the compare-at price represented before deciding whether the lamp was a bargain.
examples.zh: 我先核对了「标示的参考价」代表什么，再判断台灯划不划算。

words.enDefinition: Describes an item whose seller has reduced the previous price.

examples.en: The plain notebooks had been marked down by the time I returned from my afternoon lecture.
examples.zh: 我下午听完课回来时，素面笔记本已经「调低了售价」。

examples.en: The shelf label showed which colors of the same pencil case had been marked down.
examples.zh: 货架标签显示，同款笔袋中哪些颜色「已调低售价」。

collocations: marked down from the original price

words.enDefinition: A percentage of a stated price that is taken off the amount charged.

examples.en: The sign said ten percent off the listed price for selected backpacks that weekend.
examples.zh: 牌子写着，当周周末指定背包的标价「减免百分之十」。

examples.en: I calculated what fifteen percent off would save me on the blue lamp in the sale.
examples.zh: 我算了算，促销中的蓝色台灯「减免百分之十五」能省多少钱。

collocations: twenty percent off the listed price

words.enDefinition: A specific amount subtracted from the price of an item or order.

examples.en: The voucher gave me money off my stationery order once it reached the required amount.
examples.zh: 文具订单达到规定金额后，优惠券给了我「定额减免」。

examples.en: I compared the money off that order with the percentage discount from the other shop.
examples.zh: 我把那个订单的「定额减免」和另一家店的按比例折扣作了比较。

collocations: take money off the listed price

words.enDefinition: Half of the amount normally charged for the item.

examples.en: The notebooks with plain covers were half price when the shop cleared the display table.
examples.zh: 店铺清理陈列台时，素面笔记本卖「半价」。

examples.en: I bought the pencil case for half price at the sale after my afternoon class.
examples.zh: 下午下课后，我在促销活动中以「半价」买了这个笔袋。

words.enDefinition: A sale claim saying the largest advertised reduction is half of the stated price.

examples.en: The banner said “Up to 50% off” above a list of desks with different discounts.
examples.zh: 横幅写着「最高减免50%」，下面列的是折扣力度各不相同的书桌。

examples.en: I saw “Up to 50% off” and checked the actual price of my chosen model.
examples.zh: 我看到「最高减免50%」，随后查看了选中型号的实际价格。

collocations: a banner reading up to 50% off
a sale marked up to 50% off

words.enDefinition: Introduces the lowest advertised price among a group of items or options.

examples.en: The advert said “Prices start at ten dollars” above the selection of tablet cases.
examples.zh: 平板保护套选项上方的广告写着「价格低至十美元」。

examples.en: The line reading “Prices start at” referred to the smallest size shown on the page.
examples.zh: 写着「价格低至」的一行指的是页面上最小的尺寸。

collocations: a banner saying prices start at
prices start at the base rate

words.enDefinition: An offer giving a second qualifying product free when one is bought.

examples.en: The bookstore advertised “Buy one get one free” on a display of matching notebooks.
examples.zh: 书店在陈列成套笔记本的区域挂出了「买一送一」的广告。

examples.en: My roommate and I used a buy one get one free offer to get two pencil cases.
examples.zh: 我和室友用「买一送一」的优惠买了两个笔袋。

collocations: a buy one get one free offer
a buy one get one free sticker
advertise buy one get one free

words.enDefinition: An offer giving a lower price for buying multiple eligible items together.

examples.en: The multibuy offer made sense because our study group needed six folders of the same size.
examples.zh: 自习小组需要六个同样大小的文件夹，所以用「多买优惠」合适。

examples.en: I read the multibuy offer carefully to learn whether different colors counted toward the deal.
examples.zh: 我仔细看了「多买优惠」，想知道不同颜色能不能算在同一单里。

words.enDefinition: A package that contains extra product as part of a promotion.

examples.en: The bonus pack contained more drawing paper, but I checked the dimensions before buying it.
examples.zh: 「加量促销装」里有更多绘图纸，不过我买之前先核对了尺寸。

examples.en: I chose the bonus pack because my roommate and I could share the extra pens.
examples.zh: 我选了「加量促销装」，因为额外的笔可以和室友分着用。

collocations: compare a bonus pack with a regular pack

words.enDefinition: A better version or higher service level offered at no additional charge.

examples.en: The printing shop offered a free upgrade to thicker paper for our exhibition posters.
examples.zh: 印刷店给我们的展览海报提供了「免费升级」，可以用更厚的纸。

examples.en: I checked what the free upgrade included before ordering a display board for class.
examples.zh: 给课堂订展示板前，我先核对了「免费升级」包括什么。

collocations: a free upgrade to the larger size

words.enDefinition: A free item included when a purchase meets the stated offer conditions.

examples.en: The shop offered a gift with purchase when I bought the larger pack of markers.
examples.zh: 我买大包装马克笔时，店铺提供了一份「购物赠品」。

examples.en: A small pouch appeared as the gift with purchase on the checkout screen that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，一只小收纳袋作为「购物赠品」出现在结算页面上。

collocations: a gift with purchase of a calculator

words.enDefinition: A sale that lasts for a very short time.

examples.en: The flash sale started during our evening lecture, so I looked at the products afterward.
examples.zh: 「短时抢购活动」开始时我们在上晚课，所以我下课后才去看商品。

examples.en: I found the lamp in a flash sale that lasted just a few hours.
examples.zh: 我在只持续了几个小时的「短时抢购活动」中找到了那盏台灯。

words.enDefinition: A deal available only for a stated or brief period.

examples.en: I checked the closing time of the limited-time offer before choosing notebooks for the project.
examples.zh: 为项目选笔记本前，我查看了「限时优惠」的结束时间。

examples.en: The shop described the lamp bundle as a limited-time offer in its email this morning.
examples.zh: 店铺在今天上午的邮件中将台灯组合标成「限时优惠」。

words.enDefinition: A sale covering a broad range of items throughout a store.

examples.en: A storewide sale was advertised, so I checked which products were excluded in the smaller print.
examples.zh: 店铺打出了「全店促销」广告，我查看了小字里哪些商品除外。

examples.en: I picked up a lamp and some notebooks during the storewide sale near campus.
examples.zh: 我在校区附近的「全店促销」活动中买了台灯和几本笔记本。

words.enDefinition: A sale held as a selling season comes to an end.

examples.en: I found a lightweight blanket in an end-of-season sale while preparing for my move.
examples.zh: 准备搬家时，我在一场「季末促销」中找到了轻便的毯子。

examples.en: The end-of-season sale included the remaining summer bags, which were displayed near the shop door.
examples.zh: 「季末促销」包括剩下的夏季包袋，店里把它们摆在门口附近。

collocations: buy something in the end-of-season sale

words.enDefinition: Describes a type of product being phased out of a seller's range.

examples.en: An end-of-line lamp was cheaper than the new model, but the colors were more limited.
examples.zh: 一款「即将停售的」台灯比新款便宜，但颜色选择更少。

examples.en: The shop grouped end-of-line products on a separate shelf beside the stationery counter.
examples.zh: 商店把「即将停售的」产品集中放在文具柜台旁的单独货架上。

words.enDefinition: A sale held because a shop is about to shut permanently.

examples.en: A closing-down sale started at the small stationery shop across from my residence hall.
examples.zh: 我宿舍楼对面的小文具店开始了「歇业清仓」。

examples.en: I bought spare notebook covers during a closing-down sale at the shop near my bus stop.
examples.zh: 我在公交站旁的店铺「歇业清仓」时买了些备用笔记本封套。

words.enDefinition: A sale aimed at people buying supplies for a new school term.

examples.en: I looked through the back-to-school sale for a calculator and a pack of folders.
examples.zh: 我浏览了「开学季促销」，想买一台计算器和一包文件夹。

examples.en: Our campus bookstore advertised its back-to-school sale on a board near the main entrance.
examples.zh: 校园书店在主入口附近的牌子上打出了「开学季促销」的广告。

words.enDefinition: A prominent strip on a website or sign that advertises a discount.

examples.en: A discount banner at the top of the page linked to the eligible stationery.
examples.zh: 页面顶部的「折扣横幅」链接到参加活动的文具。

examples.en: The discount banner stayed on the page even after I changed the selected color.
examples.zh: 即便我改了所选颜色，「折扣横幅」仍然显示在页面上。

words.enDefinition: A look at products or deals before the sale officially starts.

examples.en: I browsed the sale preview to see whether the calculator I needed would be included.
examples.zh: 我浏览了「促销预览」，想看需要的计算器是否会参加活动。

examples.en: The sale preview showed discounted folders and listed when the promotion would go live online.
examples.zh: 「促销预览」展示了将打折的文件夹，还列出了活动何时在网上开始。

collocations: find something in the sale preview

words.enDefinition: A sale held as part of the shopping event known as Black Friday.

examples.en: I tracked the lamp's price for a week before checking the Black Friday sale.
examples.zh: 在查看「黑色星期五促销」前，我跟踪了一周这款台灯的价格。

examples.en: The small backpack was included in the Black Friday sale, according to the store's email.
examples.zh: 按店铺邮件，小号背包参加「黑色星期五促销」。

collocations: a Black Friday sale on electronics

words.enDefinition: An offer tied to the shopping event known as Cyber Monday.

examples.en: The Cyber Monday deal brought the blue headphones within the amount I planned to spend.
examples.zh: 「网络星期一优惠」让蓝色耳机降到了我计划花费的额度内。

examples.en: I saved the Cyber Monday deal for later because I needed to check the laptop model.
examples.zh: 我先收藏了「网络星期一优惠」，因为还需要核对笔记本电脑型号。

collocations: a Cyber Monday deal on laptops

words.enDefinition: An offer available through a website or app and unavailable in the shop itself.

examples.en: The online-only offer appeared on the website but the campus shop still displayed the usual price.
examples.zh: 网站有这项「仅限网上的优惠」，校园店铺仍显示平时的价格。

examples.en: My roommate used an online-only offer for the same notebook she had examined in class.
examples.zh: 室友用了「仅限网上的优惠」买下和她上课时看过的同款笔记本。

words.enDefinition: A label stating that an offer or item is available only at physical stores.

examples.en: The wording “In-store only” explained why I could not apply the offer to my online cart.
examples.zh: 「仅限店内」说明了为什么我不能把优惠用在网上的购物车里。

examples.en: I read “In-store only” beneath the voucher and checked when the local branch opened.
examples.zh: 我在券的下方看到「仅限店内」，就查了本地分店何时开门。

words.enDefinition: A label saying that an offer applies during the current day only.

examples.en: The message “Today only” was displayed beside the discounted folders on the bookstore's homepage.
examples.zh: 书店首页上，打折文件夹的旁边显示着「仅限今日」。

examples.en: I noticed “Today only” on the window while waiting for my friend after class.
examples.zh: 我下课后等朋友时，留意到橱窗上写着「仅限今日」。

words.enDefinition: An announcement that an offer or discounted stock is about to become unavailable.

examples.en: The sale page called it a last chance to buy the organizer at that price.
examples.zh: 促销页称，这是以这个价格买收纳盒的「最后机会」。

examples.en: I saw the last chance banner after the store added an end date to the deal.
examples.zh: 店铺给促销加了截止日期后，我看到了「最后机会」横幅。

words.enDefinition: The time for which a particular deal or campaign is offered.

examples.en: The promotional period ended before the weekend, even though the product remained on the same page.
examples.zh: 「促销期间」在周末前结束，商品却仍然留在同一个页面上。

examples.en: I checked the promotional period before telling my project group about the discounted folders.
examples.zh: 向项目小组介绍打折文件夹前，我查看了「促销期间」。

words.enDefinition: A deal giving buyers a temporary advantage, such as a lower price or an extra item.

examples.en: The shop posted a special offer on the folders we needed for the group presentation.
examples.zh: 店铺为我们小组展示需要的文件夹发布了「特别优惠」。

examples.en: I found a special offer that included spare clips with the planner I had chosen.
examples.zh: 我发现一项「特别优惠」，我选的手账会随附备用夹子。

collocations: take advantage of a special offer

words.enDefinition: A label introducing the final date for which a stated price remains in effect.

examples.en: The tag said “Price valid through Friday” below the amount printed in larger letters.
examples.zh: 标签在大字标出的金额下方写着「标价有效至星期五」。

examples.en: The webpage listed “Price valid through June” beside the specific notebook design we needed.
examples.zh: 网页在我们需要的那款笔记本旁写着「标价有效至六月底」。

collocations: mark a price valid through June
a label reading price valid through

words.enDefinition: A code a shopper enters to receive a particular offer.

examples.en: I copied the promo code from the welcome email before ordering my notebook that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上订笔记本前，我从欢迎邮件里复制了「促销码」。

examples.en: The promo code worked for one color of the lamp but had no effect on the other.
examples.zh: 「促销码」对台灯的一种颜色有效，但对另一种没有作用。

words.enDefinition: To submit a promotion code so it can be checked and used on an order.

examples.en: I waited to apply a code until I had checked which notebook sizes it covered.
examples.zh: 我确认它适用于哪些尺寸的笔记本后，才「使用优惠码」。

examples.en: The page let me apply a code before I selected the delivery method for my order.
examples.zh: 页面允许我先「使用优惠码」，再为订单选择配送方式。

collocations: a box to apply a code

words.enDefinition: A status showing that a code has been accepted for the current purchase.

examples.en: The cart showed “Code applied” beside the smaller amount for the set of folders.
examples.zh: 购物车在价格调低后的文件夹套装旁显示「优惠码已生效」。

examples.en: I noticed “Code applied” only after checking the updated price beneath my selected products.
examples.zh: 我查看了所选商品下方更新后的价格，才注意到「优惠码已生效」。

collocations: see code applied in the cart

words.enDefinition: A promotion code that the shop does not accept for the attempted use.

examples.en: The invalid code message appeared because I had copied a space at the end.
examples.zh: 我复制时带上了末尾的空格，所以页面提示「无效优惠码」。

examples.en: I saw an invalid code warning when I tried to use the online offer in the app.
examples.zh: 我尝试在应用里用网站优惠时，看到「无效优惠码」提示。

words.enDefinition: A promotion code that is past its stated period of use.

examples.en: I had copied an expired code from an email sent just before my exams.
examples.zh: 我从考试前刚收到的一封邮件里复制了一个「已过期的优惠码」。

examples.en: The shop's message said I had entered an expired code when I updated the cart.
examples.zh: 我更新购物车时，店铺提示我输入了「已过期的优惠码」。

words.enDefinition: A promotion code that can be redeemed only once.

examples.en: The store sent a single-use code with the email announcing the winter notebook sale.
examples.zh: 店铺在通知冬季笔记本促销的邮件里附了一个「一次性优惠码」。

examples.en: I saved the single-use code until I knew which case would fit my tablet.
examples.zh: 我先留着「一次性优惠码」，等确定哪个保护套适合我的平板再用。

collocations: a single-use code for an order

words.enDefinition: To use a voucher to receive the offered price, item, or other benefit.

examples.en: I tried to redeem a voucher when I bought the larger folder after class.
examples.zh: 下课后买大号文件夹时，我试着「使用优惠券」。

examples.en: The site explained where to redeem a voucher for a free notebook with my order.
examples.zh: 网站说明了在哪里「使用优惠券」，给订单加一本免费笔记本。

collocations: redeem a voucher at the store
redeem a voucher before it expires

words.enDefinition: To select and save a digital coupon so it can be used later.

examples.en: I had to clip a coupon in the app before the smaller price appeared.
examples.zh: 我得先在应用里「领取优惠券」，较低的价格才会显示。

examples.en: My roommate showed me where to clip a coupon for the cheaper laundry supplies.
examples.zh: 室友指给我看，在哪里可以「领取优惠券」买到更便宜的洗衣用品。

collocations: clip a coupon in the app

words.enDefinition: A coupon saved, displayed, or redeemed electronically instead of on paper.

examples.en: The digital coupon appeared in the shop's app below the image of the lamp.
examples.zh: 「电子优惠券」出现在店铺应用里那张台灯图片的下方。

examples.en: I used a digital coupon for the folder and kept the receipt for our group.
examples.zh: 我用了「电子优惠券」买文件夹，并给小组留着收据。

collocations: show a digital coupon on your phone

words.enDefinition: A small book containing several coupons for different offers.

examples.en: A student volunteer handed me a coupon booklet before the start of the campus fair.
examples.zh: 校园集市开始前，一名学生志愿者给了我一本「优惠券册」。

examples.en: The coupon booklet included offers from several shops within walking distance of our residence.
examples.zh: 「优惠券册」里有几家从宿舍走路就能到的店铺的优惠。

collocations: find a voucher in a coupon booklet

words.enDefinition: A discount the system applies without a shopper entering a code.

examples.en: An automatic discount appeared after I added the matching set of pens to the cart.
examples.zh: 我把配套的那套笔加入购物车后，页面显示了「自动减免」。

examples.en: The store applied an automatic discount to the online order for my project supplies.
examples.zh: 店铺给我网购项目用品的订单做了「自动减免」。

collocations: an automatic discount in the cart

words.enDefinition: To use more than one eligible discount on the same purchase.

examples.en: I checked whether the bookstore would let me stack discounts on the calculator I needed.
examples.zh: 我想买那台计算器，先查了书店是否允许「叠加使用折扣」。

examples.en: The site let me stack discounts for two promotions on the same stationery order.
examples.zh: 网站允许我在同一个文具订单上把两个活动的「折扣叠加使用」。

words.enDefinition: Says that an offer may not be used together with other offers.

examples.en: The email said the coupon cannot be combined with the discount on the product page.
examples.zh: 邮件说，这张优惠券与商品页上的折扣「不可叠加使用」。

examples.en: I spotted “Cannot be combined” below the offer when checking the new total in my cart.
examples.zh: 我核对购物车的新总额时，在优惠信息下方发现了「不可叠加使用」。

collocations: cannot be combined with other offers
a note saying cannot be combined
marked cannot be combined with discounts

words.enDefinition: A rule allowing only one coupon on each order.

examples.en: The checkout said “One coupon per order” just below the box for entering a code.
examples.zh: 结算页面的优惠码输入框正下方写着「每单限用一张优惠券」。

examples.en: My roommate noticed “One coupon per order” before trying to use our second voucher.
examples.zh: 室友准备使用第二张券之前，看到了「每单限用一张优惠券」。

collocations: a rule saying one coupon per order
limit shoppers to one coupon per order

words.enDefinition: A rule allowing each customer to use an offer on just one occasion.

examples.en: The note said “One use per customer” below the first week of term offer.
examples.zh: 开学第一周的优惠下方写着「每位顾客限用一次」。

examples.en: We read “One use per customer” before deciding who would buy the project supplies.
examples.zh: 我们看到「每位顾客限用一次」，再决定由谁来买项目用品。

collocations: a rule marked one use per customer
limit an offer to one use per customer

words.enDefinition: Restricts an offer to the first order a person places with a seller.

examples.en: The shop listed the code as “First order only” beneath its welcome offer.
examples.zh: 店铺在新客优惠下方为优惠码注明「仅限首单」。

examples.en: I noticed the message “First order only” after opening the offer from our orientation booklet.
examples.zh: 我打开迎新手册里的优惠后，注意到「仅限首单」。

collocations: an offer marked first order only
a code valid for first order only
a message saying first order only

words.enDefinition: Restricts an offer to the specific products listed or marked by the seller.

examples.en: The label “Selected items only” explained why the larger desk lamp was still full price.
examples.zh: 「仅限指定商品」的标牌说明了为什么大号台灯仍按原价卖。

examples.en: I saw “Selected items only” above the picture of the discounted pen set online.
examples.zh: 我在网上打折套笔的图片上方看到了「仅限指定商品」。

collocations: a sign reading selected items only
an offer marked selected items only
a sale on selected items only

words.enDefinition: A reduction applied to the combined price of the eligible order rather than a single item.

examples.en: The code gave us a discount on the whole order for the group project.
examples.zh: 使用优惠码后，小组项目的采购享受了「整单折扣」。

examples.en: I checked whether the discount on the whole order applied to the gift wrapping too.
examples.zh: 我核对了一下「整单折扣」是否也适用于礼品包装。

collocations: offer a discount on the whole order
get a discount on the whole order
apply a discount on the whole order

words.enDefinition: a purchase meeting the stated conditions of a promotion

examples.en: The offer required a qualifying purchase from the school supplies section that week.
examples.zh: 那一周，要参加活动得在学习用品区完成一笔「符合促销条件的消费」。

examples.en: I checked whether the notebooks counted as a qualifying purchase for the weekend deal.
examples.zh: 我查了买这些笔记本算不算周末活动的「符合促销条件的消费」。

words.enDefinition: A notice saying that some products or circumstances are excluded from an offer.

examples.en: The window sign said “Exclusions apply” underneath the line about discounted stationery for students.
examples.zh: 橱窗告示在面向学生的文具折扣下面注明「部分情况不适用」。

examples.en: I opened the details after seeing “Exclusions apply” beside the website's offer for headphones.
examples.zh: 我在网站的耳机优惠旁看到「部分情况不适用」，就打开了详情。

collocations: read exclusions apply in the small print

words.enDefinition: A condition excluding products already reduced in price from a separate offer.

examples.en: The coupon was marked “Not valid on sale items” below the store's name.
examples.zh: 优惠券在店名下方注明「不适用于打折商品」。

examples.en: I read “Not valid on sale items” before trying the code on a discounted lamp.
examples.zh: 我准备给打折台灯用优惠码时，看到了「不适用于打折商品」。

collocations: a voucher marked not valid on sale items
a code that is not valid on sale items
read not valid on sale items

words.enDefinition: Brands whose products are outside the terms of a promotion.

examples.en: The list of excluded brands was below the offer, along with the dates it ran.
examples.zh: 「不参加活动的品牌」列表和优惠日期都放在优惠文字下方。

examples.en: I checked the excluded brands to see whether my usual notebook was part of the sale.
examples.zh: 我查看了「不参加活动的品牌」，想知道自己常买的笔记本是否参加促销。

words.enDefinition: The stores where a particular campaign or offer is available.

examples.en: I checked the list of participating stores before walking to the shop near campus.
examples.zh: 走去校园附近那家店之前，我先查看了「参与活动的店铺」名单。

examples.en: The voucher was accepted at participating stores, including the branch next to my bus stop.
examples.zh: 优惠券在「参与活动的店铺」可用，公交站旁那家分店也参加。

words.enDefinition: An offer condition limiting availability to the stock set aside for it.

examples.en: The sign said the free notebooks were available while supplies last at the campus fair.
examples.zh: 告示写着，校园集市的免费笔记本「送完为止」。

examples.en: I noticed “While supplies last” beneath the offer on the stationery store's website.
examples.zh: 我在文具店网站优惠信息的下方看到「送完或售完为止」。

collocations: an offer running while supplies last
a sign reading while supplies last

words.enDefinition: The stated rules that determine when and how a coupon can be used.

examples.en: I checked the coupon terms before adding the two notebooks to my order online.
examples.zh: 在网上把两本笔记本加进订单前，我先核对了「优惠券使用条款」。

examples.en: The coupon terms explained why the offer did not cover the larger calculator case.
examples.zh: 「优惠券使用条款」解释了为什么这项优惠不适用于大号计算器保护套。

words.enDefinition: A condition stating that the benefit offered cannot be exchanged for money.

examples.en: The voucher stated “No cash alternative” below the picture of the free pencil case.
examples.zh: 优惠券在免费笔袋的图片下方注明了「不可折现」。

examples.en: I noticed “No cash alternative” in the small print under the welcome offer.
examples.zh: 我在新客优惠下的小字里留意到「不可折现」。

collocations: a note saying no cash alternative
an offer marked no cash alternative
a voucher with no cash alternative

words.enDefinition: Important conditions printed in smaller text below or beside the main offer.

examples.en: The fine print said the free pouch was available only with the larger set.
examples.zh: 「小字条款」写着，只有买大套装才会附送小包。

examples.en: I read the fine print because the voucher showed a different total from my estimate.
examples.zh: 优惠券显示的总额和我估算的不一样，所以我读了「小字条款」。

words.enDefinition: A label introducing the last date for using a coupon or offer.

examples.en: The voucher said “Redeem by Friday” underneath the instructions for claiming the free notebook.
examples.zh: 优惠券在领取免费笔记本的说明下方写着「最迟于星期五兑换」。

examples.en: I checked the “Redeem by” date before putting the paper voucher in my desk drawer.
examples.zh: 把纸质券放进书桌抽屉前，我看了「最迟兑换日期」。

collocations: a voucher marked redeem by Friday
a label saying redeem by June

words.enDefinition: A label introducing the date or time when an offer first applies.

examples.en: The website said the discount was valid from Monday, the first day of classes.
examples.zh: 网站写着折扣「自星期一起有效」，那天是开课第一天。

examples.en: I saw “Valid from noon” on the offer next to the campus bookshop entrance.
examples.zh: 我在校园书店入口旁的优惠告示上看到「自中午起有效」。

collocations: a voucher marked valid from Friday
a notice saying valid from noon

words.enDefinition: The smallest number of items needed to order something or qualify for an offer.

examples.en: The minimum quantity was three folders, so I asked if my classmates needed extras.
examples.zh: 「最低购买数量」是三个文件夹，所以我问同学还要不要多买几个。

examples.en: I checked the minimum quantity before choosing the smaller notebook design for our team.
examples.zh: 为小组选小号笔记本款式前，我查看了「最低购买数量」。

words.enDefinition: An offer instruction allowing the shopper to choose any two qualifying items.

examples.en: The sign said “Buy any two” above the shelf of notebooks with matching covers.
examples.zh: 摆了同款封面笔记本的货架上方，牌子写着「任选两件」。

examples.en: We checked which pens were included before using the “Buy any two” offer online.
examples.zh: 在网上用「任选两件」的优惠之前，我们查了哪些笔可以参加。

collocations: a sign reading buy any two

words.enDefinition: The amount of money a voucher represents when applied to a purchase.

examples.en: The voucher value appeared in large print below the name of the shopping event.
examples.zh: 购物活动名称下方用大字标出了「券面金额」。

examples.en: I checked the voucher value before working out what I still needed to pay.
examples.zh: 我先查看了「券面金额」，再算自己还要付多少钱。

words.enDefinition: The sum of money taken off the cost of an order.

examples.en: The discount amount appeared as a separate line below the names of the two folders.
examples.zh: 「优惠减免金额」单独列在两个文件夹名称的下方。

examples.en: I checked the discount amount after removing a small notebook from my online cart.
examples.zh: 我从网上购物车里移除一本小笔记本后，查看了「优惠减免金额」。

words.enDefinition: A lower price available to buyers who meet a seller's student eligibility terms.

examples.en: I asked whether the student discount applied to the calculator required for my statistics class.
examples.zh: 我问统计课要求买的计算器能不能用「学生折扣」。

examples.en: The shop listed the student discount separately from the offers available to its other customers.
examples.zh: 店铺把「学生折扣」和向其他顾客提供的优惠分开列了出来。

words.enDefinition: A label saying that a student identification card is needed to qualify.

examples.en: The placard said “Student ID required” underneath the offer for the smaller scientific calculator.
examples.zh: 告示在小号科学计算器的优惠下方写着「须出示学生证」。

examples.en: I saw “Student ID required” in the promotion details and checked what documents were accepted.
examples.zh: 我在活动详情看到「须出示学生证」，就查看了可以用哪些证件。

collocations: an offer marked student ID required
a sign saying student ID required
read student ID required in the terms

words.enDefinition: A promotion intended for someone new to a shop or service.

examples.en: The shop sent a welcome offer after I signed up to receive its email updates.
examples.zh: 我订阅邮件动态后，店铺发来一项「新客优惠」。

examples.en: I saved the welcome offer until I knew which supplies we needed for the project.
examples.zh: 我把「新客优惠」留了下来，等确定项目需要哪些用品再用。

collocations: a welcome offer for new customers

words.enDefinition: A discount offered to shoppers who sign up for or receive a seller's email newsletter.

examples.en: I used a newsletter discount from the email that announced the new stationery range.
examples.zh: 我用了文具上新邮件里的「订阅邮件优惠」。

examples.en: The site advertised a newsletter discount beside the form for signing up to receive emails.
examples.zh: 网站在邮件订阅表单旁宣传「订阅邮件优惠」。

words.enDefinition: A reduction offered for buying or booking before an early deadline.

examples.en: Our department announced an early bird discount on the printed field guides for next term.
examples.zh: 我们院系公布了下学期纸质实地指南的「提前购买优惠」。

examples.en: I bought the workshop materials before the early bird discount ended on the campus website.
examples.zh: 我赶在校园网站上的「提前购买优惠」结束前买了研讨活动的材料。

collocations: an early bird discount before Friday

words.enDefinition: A price reduction offered for placing an order before the item's general release.

examples.en: The bookstore advertised a preorder discount for the new edition of the drawing guide.
examples.zh: 书店为新版绘画指南宣传「预购折扣」。

examples.en: I checked the publication date before choosing whether to use the preorder discount on the textbook.
examples.zh: 我先查看了出版日期，再决定要不要用这本教材的「预购折扣」。

collocations: a preorder discount on the new edition

words.enDefinition: A repayment a buyer can claim by sending the required materials through the post.

examples.en: The label mentioned a mail-in rebate, so I read the conditions for claiming it.
examples.zh: 标签上提到了「邮寄申请返款」，所以我读了申领条件。

examples.en: I compared the price of the headphones with and without the advertised mail-in rebate.
examples.zh: 我分别比较了把广告上的「邮寄申请返款」算进去和不算进去时的耳机价格。

words.enDefinition: A rebate deducted from the purchase amount at the time of purchase.

examples.en: The instant rebate appeared in the summary for the printer before I submitted the order.
examples.zh: 我提交订单前，打印机的订单摘要里显示了「即时减免」。

examples.en: I saw an instant rebate on the larger model when comparing prices after class.
examples.zh: 下课后比价时，我看到大款型号有「即时减免」。

words.enDefinition: A form buyers may need to fill in to request an advertised rebate.

examples.en: The shop linked to a rebate form under the specifications for the small printer.
examples.zh: 店铺在小型打印机规格下方附上了「返款申请表」链接。

examples.en: I opened the rebate form to see which model numbers were covered by the offer.
examples.zh: 我打开「返款申请表」，想看看活动包括哪些型号。

words.enDefinition: A promotion that may return part of an eligible purchase amount to the buyer.

examples.en: The cashback offer was listed separately beneath the amount the store charged for the headphones.
examples.zh: 「购物返现优惠」单独写在店铺收取的耳机价格下方。

examples.en: I checked the terms of the cashback offer before comparing it with a lower upfront price.
examples.zh: 我先查看「购物返现优惠」的条款，再拿它和较低的直接售价比较。

words.enDefinition: Standard delivery for which the shopper is not charged a shipping fee.

examples.en: The cart offered free standard shipping for the folders but listed a charge for faster delivery.
examples.zh: 购物车显示文件夹「标准配送免运费」，更快的配送则要收费。

examples.en: I chose free standard shipping because I already had enough paper for this week's class.
examples.zh: 因为这周上课用的纸已经够了，我选了「标准配送免运费」。

words.enDefinition: A small amount or example of a product offered at no charge.

examples.en: The campus art shop offered a free sample of the paper next to its notebooks.
examples.zh: 校园美术用品店在笔记本旁提供了一份这种纸的「免费试用品」。

examples.en: A free sample of the hand cream was attached to the display card in the shop.
examples.zh: 店内展示卡上附有一份护手霜的「免费试用品」。

words.enDefinition: A small package size intended for trying a product before buying a larger amount.

examples.en: I bought the trial size because I wanted to test the ink before buying more.
examples.zh: 我买了「试用规格」，因为想先试试这款墨水，再多买些。

examples.en: The shop offered a trial size of the hand cream beside the larger bottle.
examples.zh: 店铺在大瓶旁摆了相同护手霜的「试用规格」。

collocations: a trial size of a product

words.enDefinition: An offer making the lowest-priced qualifying item in a group free.

examples.en: The sign said “Cheapest item free” above a selection of three different notebook sizes.
examples.zh: 三种大小的笔记本上方，告示写着「最便宜的一件免费」。

examples.en: I checked which pencil case counted under the “Cheapest item free” offer before checking out.
examples.zh: 结算前，我确认了「最便宜的一件免费」优惠中，哪个笔袋算免费。

collocations: an offer marked cheapest item free
a sign saying cheapest item free
buy three with the cheapest item free

words.enDefinition: A price label saying that two qualifying items cost five units of the stated currency.

examples.en: The sign said “Two for five” with a dollar symbol beside the small notebooks.
examples.zh: 小号笔记本旁的展示牌带有美元符号，写着「两件共五美元」。

examples.en: I read the “Two for five” label before picking two matching folders for our report.
examples.zh: 为报告选两个相配的文件夹之前，我看了「两件合计五元」的价格标签。

collocations: a sign saying two for five

words.enDefinition: Advertises larger savings when a shopper buys more qualifying items.

examples.en: The site said “Buy more, save more” above the pens included in the deal.
examples.zh: 网站在参加活动的笔上方写着「买得越多省得越多」。

examples.en: I read “Buy more, save more” before checking how the discount changed with the quantity.
examples.zh: 我看到「买得越多省得越多」后，去查看折扣如何随数量变化。

collocations: a banner saying “buy more, save more”

words.enDefinition: An additional amount or percentage taken off a price or an existing offer.

examples.en: The page showed an extra discount after I selected the larger pack for our group.
examples.zh: 我选了给小组用的大包装后，页面显示有「额外折扣」。

examples.en: I checked whether the extra discount also applied to the blue version of the lamp.
examples.zh: 我核对了一下「额外折扣」是否也适用于蓝色款台灯。

collocations: an extra discount on selected items

words.enDefinition: The combined amount saved through the discounts or reductions shown.

examples.en: The total savings in my cart changed when I removed the second pack of paper.
examples.zh: 我移除第二包纸后，购物车里的「总节省金额」变了。

examples.en: I checked the total savings before comparing the offer with the price at the campus store.
examples.zh: 把优惠和校园商店的价格作比较前，我查看了「总节省金额」。

words.enDefinition: The reduction actually achieved after accounting for the way an offer is applied.

examples.en: The effective discount was smaller because only one of the two folders qualified for the offer.
examples.zh: 两个文件夹中只有一个符合优惠条件，所以「实际折扣幅度」更小。

examples.en: I calculated the effective discount after checking which reductions could be used together on the order.
examples.zh: 我核对了订单上哪些减免能叠加后，算出了「实际折扣幅度」。

collocations: an effective discount of ten percent

words.enDefinition: The amount a seller charges for an item purchased through its website or app.

examples.en: I checked the online price while standing beside the same lamp in the campus shop.
examples.zh: 我在校园店看到同款台灯时，查了它的「线上售价」。

examples.en: The online price was lower for the green folder, although the shelf label showed no reduction.
examples.zh: 绿色文件夹的「线上售价」较低，但货架标签没有显示降价。

collocations: compare the online price with the shelf label

words.enDefinition: The price displayed near an item on a store shelf.

examples.en: I took a photo of the shelf price before asking which folders were included in the offer.
examples.zh: 我先拍下「货架标价」，再询问哪些文件夹参加优惠。

examples.en: The shelf price applied to the smaller pack of paper on the next row.
examples.zh: 「货架标价」适用于下一排的小包装纸。

collocations: a difference between the shelf price and the receipt

words.enDefinition: The amount shown by a store system after an item's barcode is scanned.

examples.en: The scanned price for the notebook was higher than the amount shown on the shelf label.
examples.zh: 笔记本「扫码显示的价格」高于货架标签上的金额。

examples.en: I used the shop's price scanner to check the scanned price before walking to the counter.
examples.zh: 去柜台前，我用店里的查价机查看了「扫码显示的价格」。

collocations: a mismatch with the scanned price

words.enDefinition: An unexpected difference between two prices shown for the same item.

examples.en: I noticed a price discrepancy between the shelf label and the amount shown at the register.
examples.zh: 我发现货架标价和收银系统显示的「价格不一致」。

examples.en: The price discrepancy disappeared when I switched the page back to the smaller size.
examples.zh: 我把页面切回较小的尺寸后，「价格不一致」的情况就消失了。

words.enDefinition: Expenses that are hard to notice at first when looking at the advertised price.

examples.en: I checked for hidden costs after noticing that the listed lamp price excluded its adapter.
examples.zh: 我发现台灯标价不含适配器后，查了查是否还有「未显明的额外费用」。

examples.en: The comparison sheet helped us spot hidden costs for the board we needed for the exhibition.
examples.zh: 对比表帮助我们发现了展览所需展板的「未显明的额外费用」。

words.enDefinition: Evidence that another eligible seller is offering the same product for less.

examples.en: I saved the current listing as proof of a lower price for the same calculator.
examples.zh: 我保存了当前商品信息，作为同款计算器「较低报价的凭证」。

examples.en: The page listed examples of proof of a lower price that shoppers could submit.
examples.zh: 网页列出了顾客可以提交的「较低报价的凭证」示例。

collocations: provide proof of a lower price
ask for proof of a lower price
show proof of a lower price

words.enDefinition: Describes a price or order amount that has not been reduced by discounts.

examples.en: The page showed the total before discounts separately from the final amount for our order.
examples.zh: 页面分别显示了「折前」总额和我们这单实际要付的金额。

examples.en: I noted the cost before discounts so I could keep a clear record for our group.
examples.zh: 我记下了「折前」费用，好给小组留一份清楚的记录。

words.enDefinition: A store rack holding items marked for clearance.

examples.en: I checked the clearance rack for a desk organizer before looking at the new arrivals.
examples.zh: 浏览新到商品前，我先去「清仓商品架」找桌面收纳架。

examples.en: The shop moved the older folders to the clearance rack near the front window.
examples.zh: 店铺把旧款文件夹移到了前窗旁的「清仓商品架」。

collocations: find an item on the clearance rack

words.enDefinition: The largest amount a promotion can take off a qualifying purchase.

examples.en: The discount cap applied even though my order included several packs of drawing paper.
examples.zh: 即使我的订单包含多包绘图纸，仍有「最高减免金额」限制。

examples.en: I noticed the discount cap after looking at the promotion below the large banner.
examples.zh: 我查看了大横幅下方的优惠信息后，留意到「最高减免金额」。

collocations: a discount cap of ten dollars

words.enDefinition: The amount a promotion says a shopper can save under its stated conditions.

examples.en: The advertised savings assumed I would buy both versions of the notebook in the set.
examples.zh: 「广告所示省款金额」是按套装内两个版本的笔记本都买来算的。

examples.en: I checked how the advertised savings were calculated before buying the pencil case and refills.
examples.zh: 我先核对「广告所示省款金额」是怎么算的，再买笔袋和替芯。

collocations: compare the advertised savings with your total

words.enDefinition: To pay the amount by which the chosen option costs more than an available credit or allowance.

examples.en: I could use the voucher and pay the difference for the larger poster board.
examples.zh: 我可以用这张券，再「补付差额」买大一点的海报板。

examples.en: My roommate agreed to pay the difference after choosing the sturdier version of the organizer.
examples.zh: 室友选了更结实的收纳架后，同意「补付差额」。

collocations: pay the difference for the larger model
